crosswalks.label: Computer and Information Research Scientists
crosswalks.rationale: The occupation covers advanced computer/information-science modeling and research relevant to formal knowledge representation, but it is much broader than ontology engineering.

crosswalks.label: Software Developers
crosswalks.rationale: Software Developers contribute implementation/integration work for ontology infrastructure and applications, but do not define the profession's conceptual/domain-semantics core.

findings.summary: No single O*NET occupation cleanly equals Ontology Engineer; the work spans advanced information-science/formal modeling and software implementation while retaining a distinct domain-semantics responsibility boundary.
method_labels: O*NET 31.0 Computer and Information Research Scientist plus Software Developer crosswalk comparison
findings.rationale: The body intentionally defines a narrower formal-knowledge profession instead of importing a whole external occupation.

findings.summary: Ontology engineering can make conceptual choices and formal consequences explicit but must not turn logical consistency, inference or convenient mappings into domain truth without domain-owner evidence.
method_labels: Occupational crosswalk plus AXM semantic-authority boundary review
findings.rationale: Because no occupation code supplies the whole boundary, domain authority must be explicit before the package is portable.

gaps_against_body.description: Make formal consistency/inference and domain truth separate authority surfaces; disputed meanings must route to domain owners instead of being canonized by ontology/reasoner output.

contradictions.description: The AXM Ontology Engineer boundary spans structures adjacent to research-science and software occupations; no exact one-code occupational equivalence is established.

nonclaims: This packet does not claim either O*NET occupation is equivalent to Ontology Engineer.
W3C RDF/OWL specification status is independently recorded in the body from current public metadata; specification text is not imported into this research packet.
No domain-truth, semantic-governance, TEST, WORKING or CANON authority is created.

high_stakes.authorization_nonclaim: This packet grants no domain, data, product, semantic-governance, standards or institutional authority.
